cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T3 answers T1 and T2 together; T5, T6, T8 open by building on the prior turn.
cells.limitation: T2 shifts to epistemics without answering T1's claim that goodwill must run both ways.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T5 introduces the silent-test trap, used in T6 and T10; T6's three motives reused in T7 and D.
cells.limitation: T10 adds little beyond T9's point that her later behaviour is the real evidence.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T8 sets equality against ease; T2 to T4 set pattern-as-evidence against inference from thin data.
cells.limitation: Nobody examines whether reciprocity can take forms other than initiating plans.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T4 Auditor narrows to 'a question, not a conclusion'; T10 Skeptic limits waiting to never minding.
cells.limitation: T6 warns the Auditor that tallying turns talk into audit; the Auditor never replies.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: E names the decisive unknown, why she doesn't initiate, and a small way to learn it.
cells.limitation: D lists testing through silence as a live alternative after T5 and T6 rejected it.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 grants the Skeptic's point before narrowing; T6 agrees on the silent test before challenging.
cells.limitation: After T4 nobody engages the Auditor's strongest point that a long pattern is itself information.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T2 names the assumption that silence reveals her view; T4 answers by narrowing, not restating.
cells.limitation: T5 asserts the cost of texting is small without testing it against the user's fatigue.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T3's observation versus evaluation and T8's friendship of pleasure fit Rosenberg and Aristotle.
cells.limitation: T7 says she calls the evenings lovely; the user, not the friend, said that.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T7 labels its motive guess 'Still, that's a bet'; T4 separates question from conclusion.
cells.limitation: T5 states 'the cost of texting is small' as fact; it is an assumption about the user.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T4 'Silence isn't a verdict, granted. I'll narrow my claim' revises without shifting goalposts.
cells.limitation: T6's audit objection to the Auditor goes unanswered; T10's concession names no cause.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A reframes: less whether to speak, more what you want the friendship to be.
cells.limitation: Whether this pattern recurs across the user's friendships, or only this one, is never raised.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T5 uses the lovely evenings to keep doing nothing a real option.
cells.limitation: T5 treats going quiet as untried, though the user's 'if I stop texting' suggests it happened.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T8 leaves equality versus ease 'yours to rank', keeping the user's priority distinct from the Auditor's.
cells.limitation: The Auditor's ideal of mutual goodwill frames T1 before the user's own wishes are asked.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T8 states the stake: a friendship of pleasure, real but lighter, versus a deeper one.
cells.limitation: T2 onward calls the friend 'she'; the user never gave a gender.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: E branches on whether it bothers you and on her response to the request.
cells.limitation: T7's shy and swamped branches get no move; duration of any quiet spell never asked.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T6 offers hurt, tiredness or fairness as alternatives; D turns them into an answerable question.
cells.limitation: T7 dismisses the tiredness motive on the misread that she called the evenings lovely.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 separates the checkable pattern from the guess 'she doesn't care'.
cells.limitation: The assumption that initiating plans is the measure of shared effort stays unexamined after T1.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T8 and D name the conflict: easy warmth or even effort.
cells.limitation: What each value would cost the user to give up is stated, not worked through.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T6 names fear of being merely tolerated and a belief friendships ought to be even.
cells.limitation: Fear of hearing an unwelcome answer when asking is touched in T4 only as hiding.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: D's self-reflection question and T8's 'yours to rank' leave the distinctions for the user to refine.
cells.limitation: D's closing question narrows to two wishes, dropping the tiredness option it just listed.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: D defines asking with curiosity, testing through silence, or accepting the rhythm; T9 a limited step.
cells.limitation: Different ways of speaking up, naming feelings versus only requesting a plan, are not distinguished.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T6 prices the silent test as punishment; T8 prices accepting as a lighter friendship.
cells.limitation: T9 and E present the small request with no cost or risk named.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: T9 and E: whether she picks the next plan after the request is observable.
cells.limitation: E's 'nothing changes over a while' sets no observable point and favours no option.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: E names why she doesn't initiate as the decisive unknown; T10 says one response won't settle it.
cells.limitation: Whether the friend initiates with other people, a key discriminator, is never raised.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: T9 gives a small script: notice you reach out first, ask her to pick the next plan.
cells.limitation: T9's script drops the feeling step T3 recommended, without saying why.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T3's 'what happened is checkable... what it means is a guess' is plain and precise.
cells.limitation: T8's 'friendship of pleasure' is a term of art glossed only as 'real but lighter'.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T6 'Agreed on the silent test' and 'warn the Auditor' point clearly to T5 and T1.
cells.limitation: T10's 'I'll concede that much' has no clear referent turn.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten turns, all within range per deterministic checks; each turn carries one move.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Auditor blunt and verdict-first (T1), Skeptic evidential (T2), Plain Speaker procedural (T3).
cells.limitation: T7's Skeptic, warning against confident stories, bets on a motive, blurring its position.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns rarely recap; D and E summarise rather than repeat lines.
cells.limitation: T10's 'give her time to act' repeats T9's 'what she does after'.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T1's 'a pleasant acquaintance who is happy to be carried' makes the stake sting.
cells.limitation: What losing or deepening this friendship would mean to the user stays abstract.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T4 narrows after T2's argument: 'Silence isn't a verdict, granted.'
cells.limitation: Reversals are mild narrowings; T10's concession names no turn that caused it.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T4's 'a very comfortable place to hide forever' gives the Auditor bite.
cells.limitation: Voices are restrained and humourless; the Plain Speaker reads as procedure more than person.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T6's 'a punishment dressed as an experiment' is sharp and apt.
cells.limitation: No concrete image or example of the friendship; delivery relies on aphorism.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: Moves from T1's verdict through doubt (T2) to branches (T8) and concession (T10).
cells.limitation: Even intensity throughout; no turn lands as a peak or emotional turn.

strengths: T6 offers hurt, tiredness and fairness as alternative motives, each needing a different conversation, and D turns them into a question.
T4 Auditor narrows his claim in response to T2 and T3, a caused revision rather than a template.
E maps observable conditions to options and T9 gives a proportionate, concrete small request.
weaknesses: T7 Skeptic credits the friend with the user's word 'lovely' and uses it to dismiss the tiredness motive.
T5 treats going quiet as untried though the user implies it happened; duration never asked.
The Skeptic and others call the friend 'she' without basis; T6's audit warning to the Auditor goes unanswered.

symptoms.observed: Attributes the user's own 'lovely' to the friend, then reasons from it.
symptoms.evidence: I doubt it's workload; she calls the evenings lovely.

symptoms.observed: Treats going quiet as hypothetical; never asks if the user already tried it.
symptoms.evidence: Then watch the other trap: going quiet to see what happens.

symptoms.observed: Gives the friend a gender the user never stated.
symptoms.evidence: You can't see what her silence means from inside her head.

symptoms.observed: Presents the small request with no cost or risk named.
symptoms.evidence: It's a request, not a charge.

symptoms.observed: Auditor never answers the warning that tallying turns talk into audit.
symptoms.evidence: I'd also warn the Auditor that tallying effort turns a talk

findings.description: States the friend calls the evenings lovely; the user's situation says the user finds them lovely.
Refers to the friend as 'she'; the user gave no gender.
Rosenberg's model has four components including needs; T3 lists observation, feeling and request only.
Attributions to Aristotle, Kahneman and Rosenberg are paraphrases consistent with the works but not checked against sources.

rubric_fit_notes: Ambiguity whether the user already stopped texting is a reading judgment; I treated the debate's hypothetical framing as a minor miss, not a material one.
raw.question_type_note: Read as a decision: whether and how to raise the imbalance, with every cell read as written.
